title: On the uniqueness of the strictly convex quadrilateral central configuration with a fixed angle

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, definition of collision set after Eq. (1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines the singular/collision set as Δ = {x ∈ R^{dn} | x_i = x_j, ∀ i ≠ j}. This describes only total collision (all bodies coincident), whereas the collision set for the n-body problem is the union over pairs i ≠ j of {x_i = x_j}. The definition omits partial collisions.

The paper claims ζ1 = R13 − 2η = m1m3/r13^3 and similarly ζ2 = m1m4/r14^3, ζ3 = m2m3/r23^3, ζ4 = m2m4/r24^3. But from (18), e.g. S13 = 2η r13 gives 2η = m1m3(δ − r13^{-3}), so R13 − 2η = m1m3(δ + 2/r13^3) − m1m3(δ − 1/r13^3) = 3m1m3/r13^3. The factor 3 is missing in all four formulas.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 2, equations for a1/a0 and the final expression for a0
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The quadratic for the (r12,r34) block has roots ζ5,ζ6 with product a0 = R12R34 − 4η^2 cos^2θ. The paper instead writes a0 = ζ5ζ6 = 4 r12^3 r13^6 r14^6 r23^6 r24^6 r34^3 (R12R34 − 4η^2 r12^3 r34^3 cos^2θ), which is dimensionally inconsistent. Moreover, correct substitution of the equations S12 + 2η r34 cosθ = 0 and S34 + 2η r12 cosθ = 0 gives a0 = 3m1m2m3m4[1 + δ(r12^3 + r34^3)]/(r12^3 r34^3), not the stated denominator-free expression. The intermediate cosθ formulas also omit the mass factors m1m2 and m3m4.

The paper defines E^5(1) = {r ∈ R^5 | Σ_{i<j} m_i m_j r_{ij}^2 = 1}. But there are six mutual distances r12,r13,r14,r23,r24,r34, so this set is a 5-dimensional ellipsoid embedded in R^6, and the vector r should be in R^6, not R^5.
The text says D1 'forms a quarter of a disk with radius 1/2'. But D1 is defined by r14^2 + r23^2 = G1 ≤ 1/2, so the radius is sqrt(1/2), not 1/2.

The text states: 'Now fix a point (r14,r23) ∈ H'. However H was just defined as H = { (r12,r34) ∈ (R^+)^2 | r12^2 + r34^2 ≤ 1 }. The fixed point should be (r12,r34), not (r14,r23). This is an incorrect variable reference in the fibration argument.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, discussion of Perpendicular Bisector Theorem
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that the Perpendicular Bisector Theorem implies 'no (n−1)-body collinearity in a planar n-body central configuration'. This is false as stated because collinear central configurations are planar and have all n bodies, hence any n−1 subset, collinear. The statement would only be valid under an additional non-collinearity assumption.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 3, final paragraph relating M0+ to M+
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof claims that M0+ ⊂ S^5(1) is homeomorphic to M+ ⊂ E^5(1) via the homeomorphism from the sphere to the mass ellipsoid, with the cone C(r)=0 preserved. The natural scaling r_ij ↦ r_ij/√(m_i m_j) does not preserve the equation C(r)=0 unless the masses are equal; it sends C=0 to a different quadratic constraint. The equality χ(M+) = χ(M0+) is therefore not justified by the argument as written.
